rookie_crew_underdog_on_production.classification_evidence: Week-blocked 95% interval [-2.6906, +0.2217] accuracy points; the upper bound sits fractionally above zero, so this is NOT a RESOLVED whole-interval-below-zero wrong sign despite the low probability_positive (0.0456) -- the admissible ground requires the WHOLE interval on the wrong side, which this narrowly misses. No positive control was run against this specific effect size (the harness leak positive control, +44.3pp P+ 1.0, proves harness sensitivity only). Left-censoring disclosed: 17/29 (58.6%) referees show a 2015 debut (censored, unknown true tenure) vs 12/29 (41.4%) genuine 2016-2025 debuts; the Stage-2 population is restricted to season >= 2016 for exactly this reason.
rookie_crew_underdog_on_production.description: LEAD-31: take the UNDERDOG when the assigned officiating crew is in its first or second dataset-visible season (season >= 2016, excludes left-censored 2015), stacked on production weak_stack, opener-graded window [2020,2021].
rookie_crew_underdog_on_production.notes: docs/officials_crew_leads.md, LEAD-31 Stage 2. Late-week refresh-channel candidate (referee assignments publish Wednesday-Thursday, after the Tuesday lock); nfl_ats.crew_tilt_refresh_overlay is the existing live vehicle for this pattern, not wired here this session.
rookie_crew_underdog_on_production.plain_summary: Taking the underdog when a first- or second-year referee crew is assigned leans slightly the WRONG way in this sample -- not proven wrong, since the interval still brushes positive, but it does not support the predeclared chaos mechanism either.
